stops.note: name of the ram-headed god whose desert oracle-temple gave salt deposits nearby his name
stops.meaning: a principal Egyptian deity, 'the hidden one'

stops.note: Greeks renamed the god Ammon and the salts mined near his Libyan temple after him; Pliny the Elder's Latin 'sal hammoniacus' carried the name into European chemistry
stops.meaning: the god, and by extension the salt from his temple's sands

stops.note: coined in scientific Latin by chemist Torbern Bergman for the pungent gas from sal ammoniac

current_meaning: A pungent, colorless alkaline gas (NH3) widely used in cleaning products, fertilizers, and industrial chemistry.
